description:
What you'll do
 
 
 Own physical implementation of accelerator blocks and top level: synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock tree synthesis, and routing

 Develop floorplans for repeated compute tiles, large SRAM arrays, and high-bandwidth data movement, balancing congestion, wire length, and utilization

 Close timing, power, and area (PPA) targets, including optimization of datapath-heavy and high-fanout structures

 Manage power delivery and density: power grid design, IR-drop and electromigration analysis, and thermal-aware implementation

 Implement low-power techniques such as clock gating, power gating, multi-Vt, and multi-voltage domains

 Run static timing analysis, signal-integrity, and physical verification (DRC/LVS) signoff across corners and modes

 Partition and implement hierarchical designs, including budgeting and integration of replicated blocks

 Work with architecture, RTL, DFT, and verification teams to co-optimize design for physical implementability

 Develop and maintain automation for flows, regressions, and QoR tracking

 Support silicon bring-up and correlate post-silicon results with pre-silicon predictions


  

 

What we're looking for
 
 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field 

 5+ years of industry experience in high performance,  low power physical design

 Hands-on experience taking complex digital designs through synthesis, place-and-route, and signoff at advanced process nodes

 Strong understanding of timing closure, clocking, and static timing analysis, including OCV and multi-corner multi-mode analysis

 Experience with power integrity: power grid design, IR drop, and electromigration

 Experience with physical verification (DRC/LVS) and fixing violations

 Familiarity with accelerator or compute-array architectures, such as systolic arrays, SIMD/vector engines, and large on-chip memories

 Proficiency with industry-standard EDA tools (see Tools & Technologies)

 Scripting skills in Tcl, Python, or Perl for flow automation

 Strong debugging skills and the ability to work with RTL, architecture, and DFT teams
